name: Tulika

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Tulika Bibidh Rang writes Hindi poetry and works across communication education and documentary film. Amity University’s faculty profile records her work in its School of Communication, her co-direction of Khanabadosh and interests in audiovisual storytelling and folk art. It dates a Pen In Books Young Author Award for her Hindi poetry manuscript Gulabi Canvas to January 2021.

In “Basanti Budget”, the language of examinations, meetings, growth and financial planning is redirected towards emotional life. Against an exhausting race for achievement, the poem proposes making room for family laughter, neighbourly food, affection and hope. Spring becomes a model of change that is generous rather than merely competitive; the budget worth balancing is one that leaves space for shared happiness.

“Beti Bachao Beti Padhao” tests a familiar public slogan against the treatment of daughters who actually grow, study and make choices. Its recurring phrase becomes an accumulating indictment: achievement is praised in principle, yet resistance to violence, independent movement and single motherhood attract suspicion. The closing turn from being cherished to fighting for affection exposes the distance between public approval and the freedom a woman is allowed at home.
